spots.name: Erasmusbrug
spots.summary: The Erasmusbrug is a combined cable-stayed and bascule bridge. Construction began in 1986 and was completed in 1996. It crosses the Nieuwe Maas in the centre of Rotterdam, connecting the north and south parts of the city.

spots.name: Museum Boijmans Van Beuningen

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: Municipal Museum Boijmans Van Beuningen is an art museum in Rotterdam in the Netherlands. The name of the museum is derived from its two most important donors, Frans Jacob Otto Boijmans and Daniël George van Beuningen.

spots.name: Euromast
spots.summary: Euromast is an observation tower in Rotterdam, Netherlands, designed by Hugh Maaskant constructed between 1958 and 1960. It was specially built for the 1960 Floriade, and is a listed monument since 2010. The tower is a concrete structure with an internal diameter of 9 m (30 ft) and a wall thickness of 30 cm (12 in).

spots.name: Grote or Sint-Laurenskerk

hours.note: Closed Mon, Sun

spots.summary: Grote Kerk or Sint-Laurenskerk is a Protestant church in Rotterdam, Netherlands. It is the only remnant of the medieval city of Rotterdam.

spots.name: Diergaarde Blijdorp
spots.summary: Diergaarde Blijdorp, officially Rotterdam Zoo, is a zoo located in the northwestern part of Rotterdam. It is one of the oldest zoos in the Netherlands, and has been operated by the Stichting Koninklijke Rotterdamse Diergaarde.

photo.author: The original uploader was Sherpa at Dutch Wikipedia.

spots.name: Witte Huis

hours.note: Closed Mon, Sun

spots.summary: The Witte Huis or White House is a building and National Heritage Site in Rotterdam, Netherlands, built in 1898 in the Art Nouveau style. The building is 43 m (141 ft) tall, with 10 floors. It was the first hoogbouw in Europe. The building is listed as a Rijksmonument.

spots.name: De Rotterdam

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: De Rotterdam is a skyscraper on the Wilhelminapier in Rotterdam, designed by the Office for Metropolitan Architecture in 1998 and developed by Edge. The complex is located between the KPN Tower and Rotterdam Cruise Terminal and was finalized at the end of 2013.

spots.name: Willemsbrug
spots.summary: The Willemsbrug is a bridge next to the Erasmusbrug in the centre of Rotterdam, Netherlands, spanning the Nieuwe Maas. It links the northern part of the city with the Noordereiland and the district of Feijenoord.

spots.name: Van Nelle Factory
spots.summary: The former Van Nelle Factory on the Schie in Rotterdam, is considered a prime example of the modernist and functionalist architecture. It has been a designated UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2014.

spots.name: Van Brienenoord Bridge
spots.summary: The Van Brienenoord Bridge is a large twin tied-arch motorway bridge in the Netherlands. Located at the east side of Rotterdam, it crosses the New Meuse , a major distributary of the river Rhine.

spots.name: Santa Claus
spots.summary: Santa Claus, popularly known as the Buttplug Gnome, is a 2001 statue by artist Paul McCarthy in the Eendrachtsplein square of Rotterdam, The Netherlands.

spots.name: The Destroyed City
spots.summary: The Destroyed City is a bronze memorial sculpture in the Dutch city of Rotterdam. It commemorates the German bombing of Rotterdam on 14 May 1940, which destroyed the medieval centre of the city. Unveiled in 1953, it was designated as a Dutch national monument (Rijksmonument) in 2010.

spots.name: De Hef
spots.summary: De Hef, officially Koningshaven Bridge, is a vertical-lift bridge over the Koningshaven channel at the port of Rotterdam, Netherlands. Built in 1927, the bridge was part of the Breda–Rotterdam railway line until it was decommissioned in 1993. Today, it is a Rijksmonument heritage site.

spots.name: Delftse Poort

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Delftse Poort is a twin-tower skyscraper complex at Weena 505 next to the Rotterdam Centraal railway station in Rotterdam, Netherlands. Tower I is 151.35 m (496.6 ft) tall and has 41 stories, while Tower II is 93 m (305 ft) tall and has 25 stories. Until May 2009, Tower I was the tallest office tower in the Netherlands.

photo.author: Paul van de Velde from Netherlands

spots.name: Maastoren

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Maastoren is with its height of 165 metres the second tallest building in the Netherlands. The office building is situated on the bank of the Nieuwe Maas, after which the building is named, in the neighborhood Kop van Zuid in the South Holland city of Rotterdam.

spots.name: Cube Houses
spots.summary: These houses, designed by Dutch architect Piet Blom, are literally cubes, tilted over by 45 degrees. There were 39 cube houses built in Rotterdam in the early 1980s, along with 18 in Helmond, and 3 in Toronto.

spots.name: Rotterdam City Hall

hours.note: Closed Sun

spots.summary: Rotterdam City Hall was built between 1914 and 1920 by Henri Evers. It is one of the few buildings in the center of Rotterdam that survived the bombing of May 14, 1940. Since 10 October 2000 it has been recognized as a Rijksmonument.

spots.name: De Zalmhaven
spots.summary: De Zalmhaven, also referred to as Zalmhaventoren, is a residential tower complex in Rotterdam, the Netherlands. The main tower of the complex, Zalmhaven I, reaches 215 metres (705 ft) in height, while the other two buildings reach 70 metres (230 ft) each. The project was approved by the city in February 2010.

spots.name: Kunsthal

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The Kunsthal is an art space in Rotterdam, the Netherlands. It opened in 1992.

spots.name: Montevideo

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Montevideo is a 43-storey, 139.5 m (458 ft) residential skyscraper on the river Nieuwe Maas in Rotterdam, The Netherlands. The Montevideo logo on the roof is an 8 by 8 m letter "M" which brings the tower's total height to 152.3 m (500 ft). The logo is also designed to be a giant wind vane.

spots.name: Coolsingel
spots.summary: Coolsingel is a street in central Rotterdam. It is located in the Cool district. The street leads from the Hofplein to the Churchillplein. Plans were announced in 2016 to reduce traffic congestion on the street. The redevelopment is expected to cost 47 million euros and to be finished by 2020.

spots.name: Schielandshuis
spots.summary: The Schielandshuis is a historic mansion in Stadsdriehoek in the center of Rotterdam, the Netherlands. This is one of the two buildings older than the 19th century which survived the 1940 German bombing of Rotterdam.

spots.name: The Red Apple

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Red Apple is a 40-storey, 124-metre (407 ft) residential skyscraper on Wijnhaven Island in Rotterdam, Netherlands, designed by KCAP Architects & Planners and Jan des Bouvrie. The building was topped out in 2008, completed in 2009, and features 121 units, and a 338-space multi-storey car park.

spots.name: Lijnbaan
spots.summary: The Lijnbaan is a pedestrian shopping street in the centre of Rotterdam, Netherlands. It was designed by Jo van den Broek and Jaap Bakema as part of the rebuilding of the city after the German bombing of 1940, and opened on 9 October 1953. It has been described as the first purpose-built pedestrian street in Europe.

spots.name: Maritime Museum Rotterdam

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The Maritime Museum Rotterdam is a maritime museum in Rotterdam, The Netherlands. Dedicated to naval history, it was founded in 1874 by Prince Henry of the Netherlands.

spots.name: FENIX Museum of Migration

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The FENIX Museum of Migration is a museum dedicated to human migration, located within the former Fenix warehouse in Rotterdam, the Netherlands. It was opened on 16 May 2025.

spots.name: Moments Contained
spots.summary: Moments Contained is a 2022-2023 bronze sculpture on the Stationsplein, in front of Rotterdam Centraal station, Rotterdam, the Netherlands. It was created by artist Thomas J Price, a London-based artist with Caribbean roots. A similar statue is on display at the Victoria and Albert Museum in London.

spots.name: St. Laurentius

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The cathedral of Rotterdam (Roman Catholic) is a somewhat heavy neo romanesque creation from 1907. The interior is quite well proportioned and atmospheric. Sunday mass is at 11:00 (sometimes with a good choir). Besides assisting at the normally well attended mass you can walk in before or after to have a look inside.

spots.name: Monsieur Jacques
spots.summary: Monsieur Jacques, also known as Meneer Jacques, is a bronze sculpture made in 1956 by the Dutch sculptor Oswald Wenckebach (1895–1962). Casts stand at the entrance of the Kröller-Müller Museum in Otterlo and, since 1959, on the Coolsingel in Rotterdam.

spots.name: Erasmus
spots.summary: The Statue of Erasmus is a public monument by Hendrick de Keyser in Rotterdam, the Netherlands.

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.name: Stormvloedkering Hollandse IJssel
spots.summary: The Stormvloedkering Hollandse IJssel, Hollandse IJsselkering or Algerakering is a storm surge barrier located on the Hollandse IJssel, at the municipal boundary of Capelle aan den IJssel and Krimpen aan den IJssel, east of Rotterdam in The Netherlands.

spots.name: World Port Center

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: World Port Centre is a 33-storey, 123.1 m (404 ft) skyscraper in Rotterdam, Netherlands.

spots.name: Maastunnel
spots.summary: The Maastunnel is a tunnel in Rotterdam, the Netherlands, connecting the banks of the Nieuwe Maas. About 75,000 motor vehicles and a large number of cyclists and pedestrians use the tunnel daily, making the Maastunnel an important part of Rotterdam's road network. Building commenced in 1937 and finished in 1942.

spots.name: Netherlands Photo Museum

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The Netherlands Photo Museum (NFM) is a photography museum in Rotterdam, the Netherlands, that was founded in 2003.

photo.author: FaceMePLS from The Hague, The Netherlands

spots.name: Arminiuskerk

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: This large work by Pablo Picasso was erected in 1973. It is one of the elaborations Picasso made based on the portraits of his muse Sylvette David. Definitely worth a look.

spots.name: Oceanium
spots.summary: The Oceanium is a public aquarium that opened in 2001 in Diergaarde Blijdorp, a zoo in Rotterdam, Netherlands. The Oceanium lies in the expansion area of the zoo, which includes a new entrance and parking area, and was the biggest project to date for the zoo.

spots.name: Beurs-World Trade Center
spots.summary: Beurs-World Trade Center is located on the Coolsingel and Beursplein in the centre of Rotterdam.

spots.name: Wereldmuseum Rotterdam

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The Wereldmuseum Rotterdam is an ethnographic museum, situated at Willemskade in Rotterdam, the Netherlands.

spots.name: Schouwburgplein
spots.summary: Theatre Square is a plaza situated in the heart of the city of Rotterdam, and is flanked by the municipal theatre, concert hall, restaurants, and cafes.

photo.author: No machine-readable author provided. Steinbach assumed (based on copyright claim

spots.name: De Doelen

hours.note: Closed Mon, Sun

spots.summary: De Doelen is a concert venue and convention centre in Rotterdam, Netherlands. It was originally built in 1934 but then destroyed in 1940 during the German bombardment of Rotterdam in May 1940 at the outset of World War II. It was rebuilt in 1966, originally with one hall to which two more were added in the 1990s.

spots.name: Chabot Museum

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The Chabot Museum is a museum dedicated to the Dutch painter and sculptor Hendrik (Henk) Chabot in Rotterdam in the Netherlands. The museum is housed in a monumental villa in the Museumpark, near the Museum Boijmans van Beuningen and the Netherlands Architecture Institute.

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.name: Timmerhuis
spots.summary: The Timmerhuis is a building complex in the Stadsdriehoek district in the center of Rotterdam. The building is a combination of post-World War II reconstruction architecture by municipal architect J.R.A. Koops and contemporary architecture by the Office for Metropolitan Architecture (OMA).

spots.name: Pilgrim Fathers Church

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Old or Pilgrim Fathers' Church is a church located in Rotterdam-Delfshaven, in the Netherlands.

spots.name: Weena
spots.summary: Weena is a street with many highrises in the center of Rotterdam, Netherlands. It defines the Rotterdam skyline. The street of about 1 kilometer length leads east-west from Hofplein to Beukelsdijk.

spots.name: De Bijenkorf
spots.summary: De Bijenkorf is a chain of high-end department stores in the Netherlands, with its flagship store on Dam Square in Amsterdam. The chain is owned by Selfridges Group, owner also of Britain's Selfridges and Ireland's Brown Thomas and Arnotts.

spots.name: Het Nieuwe Instituut

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: Nieuwe Instituut is a cultural centre in Rotterdam, the Netherlands. It focuses on architecture, design, and digital culture. NI is in a building designed by Jo Coenen at Museumpark 25 in the centre of Rotterdam, adjacent to the Museum Boijmans Van Beuningen.

spots.name: Plaswijckpark
spots.summary: Plaswijckpark is a recreational and amusement park located on the shores of the Bergse Achterplas founded in 1923 between the districts of Hillegersberg and Schiebroek on the northern edge of Rotterdam, Netherlands. The park is owned by the Stichting Plaswijckpark.

spots.name: De Kuip
spots.summary: Stadion Feijenoord, more commonly known by its nickname De Kuip, is a stadium in Rotterdam, Netherlands. It was completed in 1937. The name is derived from the Feijenoord district in Rotterdam, and from the club with the same name. The stadium has also hosted the Dutch national football team.

photo.author: Author and original uploader was ART at nl.wikipedia

spots.name: Natural History Museum Rotterdam

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The Natuurhistorisch Museum Rotterdam is a natural history museum located in Rotterdam, Netherlands.

spots.name: Hofplein
spots.summary: Hofplein is a major public town square in Rotterdam, the Netherlands. The square lies on a crossing of the Weena, the Schiekade and the Coolsingel. In the center of the square a large fountain is situated.

spots.name: Te Riviere Castle
spots.summary: Te Riviere Castle is a ruinous castle located in Schiedam, Netherlands.

spots.name: Station Rotterdam Blaak
spots.summary: The area around the station was destroyed by a Nazi bombardment during World War II, forcing the Netherlands to surrender. After the war this area was populated with some bold examples of modern architecture.

spots.name: Museum of Chess-Pieces

hours.note: Closed Mon, Tue, Thu, Fri, Sat, Sun

spots.summary: This little museum can be found among the famous Cube houses and houses a diverse collection of chess games. From ancient Chinese to all sorts of cartoon characters.

hours.note: Closed Mon
Closed Mon

photo.author: Donald Trung Quoc Don (Chữ Hán: 徵國單) - Wikimedia Commons - © CC BY-SA 4.0 Intern

spots.name: Huis Sonneveld

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: A building in the Bauhaus style built in 1932-1933 by Leendert van der Vlugt. It is now a part of the Het Nieuwe Instituut museum.

spots.name: Chinatown
spots.summary: Just walk out the front of Rotterdam Centraal Station, cross the Weena and go strait to the first intersection. You can't miss it! It is a massive Chinatown, full of Chinese restaurants but also Indonesian and other Asian restaurants.

spots.name: Oude Haven
spots.summary: The Old Harbour is a nice place to see and sit at some café nearby.

spots.name: Witte de With

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: Witte de With(Centre for Contemporary Arts) exhibits, lectures, multimedia for contemporary arts.

photo.author: Donald Trung Quoc Don (Chữ Hán: 徵國單) - Wikimedia Commons - © CC BY-SA 4.0 Intern

spots.name: Angelo Betti
spots.summary: Italian kitchen and ice cream parlour. Whether you come for a dinner or a takeaway pizza, you always have to wait. But everything here is definitely worth the wait! And what is so bad about having to wait a while when you can sit in the sun with a glass of great Italian wine in front of the restaurant? The good ingredients and the classy Italian waiters make the picture complete. In one word: fant

spots.name: Bierhandel De Pijp

hours.note: Closed Sun

spots.summary: Prepare yourself for something special when visiting this famous eatery. The outside is absolutely rundown (so is the interior) and you must convince yourself to really push open the dark door. Once inside you will be welcomed by waiters in white and you will be allocated directly next to other visitors on benches. Good food is served (traditional Dutch and French fare), cooked in the same space t

spots.name: Lokanta Dunya
spots.summary: The first floor is much like a Turkish market square. It is fully decorated and cozy, the fake balcony and window pane complete the market square. Through a small staircase you reach the 'living room'. Tip: Enjoy the fresh baked bread before you start your dinner. They have a wood stove that gives the food that extra authentic taste; some great wood-heated meals are stuffed zucchini and stuffed ko

spots.name: Restaurant Lux
spots.summary: Nicely decorated Italian restaurant where you don't just drop by for a simple pizza. As a matter of fact, they don't even serve pizza. With the fine use of herbs, garlic and more interesting stuff that the Italian kitchen has to offer, it is almost impossible to not like this food. The personal is professional and for what you get the prices are actually not too bad. In summer you can eat outside

spots.name: Café Restaurant Sijf

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Very nice old-looking bar. They also serve food for a reasonable price and most of the food is home made. Try the grilled beef with Spanish pepper and garlic! Or have one of their great sandwiches or salads. Wanna have a nice Belgium beer that gets you all fuzzy? They have an awesome Belgian beer called “la Chouffe” (the midget) on draft. Very tasty! A good start for the evening.

spots.name: Rotown

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: This is 'the' place in town for creative people. Or it used to be, because lots of people now go to the next-door café's Stalles and Parket. Rotown has a restaurant with decent food for a decent price. The daily changing menu (meat, fish and vegetarian) usually gets you something nice. After eating you can go watch a band or have your drink in the café.

spots.name: S.S. Rotterdam

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: A ship built in 1959, now permanently moored and converted to a hotel/restaurants venue. There are two fine restaurants and a bar. When the weather is nice there is a great terrace with a view. Before the F&B you can book a tour. Or even better, spend the night at this fabulous cruise ship. Guided tours around the ship are also available.

spots.name: (Cocktail) Bar-Restaurant Stockholm

hours.note: Closed Sat

spots.summary: Two of the best things in gastronomy come together at Bar-Restaurant Stockholm: A high standard yet fair priced French-inspired menu & the exquisite cocktails. Together with the trendy interior and city centre location Stockholm has been a well-earned success for years.

spots.name: Grand café Wester Paviljoen

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Rotterdammers like to read their newspaper here. For a solid breakfast (Dutch “wentelteefjes”), good lunch, or a fast meeting Westerpaviljoen is a perfect place. Hang out on their huge and fantastic terrace, drink a nice glass of Amstel or Hoegaarden White beer.

spots.name: Charly's Lunchroom

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: This restaurant/café/art society is a Rotterdam institute. Housed in a magnificent building reminiscent to a Mondriaan painting, being built in the De Stijl-style, it also hosts all kinds of cultural venues and parties. A good place to have coffee too.

spots.name: Café-Restaurant Kade 4

hours.note: Closed Sat

spots.summary: A cafe in an authentic part of the city centre: in the Old Harbour. Open all year round for lunch, dinner or just coffee and delicious cake. One of the most popular terraces during summer. Fair prices, spontaneous staff, basic French-inspired cuisine.

spots.name: Café De Witte Aap

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: This classic Rotterdam pub (The White Monkey) draws a very varied and often too large crowd for its premises. It's a cool place to have a few drinks before dinner or before exploring the rest of this very lively neighborhood.

spots.name: Stadshaven Brouwerij

hours.note: Closed Mon, Tue, Thu

spots.summary: Located in a 100-year old former fruit warehouse, this craft beer brewery is the second largest independent brewery in the Netherlands. You can also book a tour, most are in Dutch but one in English is offered on Thursday.

spots.name: Stalles

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: This café has pizzas offers on Mondays and Tuesdays. The atmosphere in the restaurant is relaxed and friendly. The menu furthermore features salads, sandwiches, and tapas. The owner also owns Club Vibes, around the corner.

spots.name: Pol Bar

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Nice looking bar with modern solid patio. Crowd can be sort of posh sometimes, but don't let that scare you to much. Right next to the market (Tuesday and Thursday), and they won some prices with their sandwiches.

spots.name: Tiki's

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Don't let the cheesy Hawaiian interior put you off. Frequented by an alternative arty crowd, with rockabilly and ska (and occasionally Ethiopian jazz) on the loudspeakers. Cocktails and small dinner menu.

spots.name: Paddy Murphy's

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: This Irish pub is really Irish. Green and wooden colors and a bar crew who only speaks English. Live music every night! On Monday there's pub bingo. In the weekends the entrance fee is €2.50.

spots.name: El Aviva

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Kapsalon is a wonderful variation of Shoarma that was invented at this restaurant in Rotterdam. It has now become famous all over the Netherlands. A delicious, greasy meal!

spots.name: Restaurant Amarone

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: A culinary gem in the very heart of the city, this stylish restaurant needs to be booked well in advance. Very rewarding French cuisine. Valet parking.

spots.name: Café 't Pakhuys

hours.note: Closed Mon, Tue

spots.summary: Claims the title of smallest pub of Delfshaven, giving it a wonderful small-scale atmosphere.
